successors.name: Roman Republic
successors.text: 'covering much of the four departments of the modern Franche-Comté': the Jura passes on the east against the Helvetii, the Saône on the west against the Aedui and Lingones; Vesontio (Besançon) in a…

ledger.x: The Sequani hold the Saône-Doubs country round Vesontio and the Jura passes.

c. 70 BC: Germanic settlers take the east. 'Germanic groups occupied part of Sequanian territory around 70 BC'; 'The Germanic king Ariovistus, whom the Sequani had called in, settled on the left bank of the Rhine and turned against his former allies'. The Ariovistus page says he took a third of the territory of the…
September 52 BC: the Sequani, who had sent 12,000 men to the coalition, fall under Rome with Alesia, which 'proved to be the end of generalized and organized resistance'.
September 52 BC: the independent Sequani end; the civitas is later incorporated into Gallia Belgica under Augustus.

wars.name: Gallic Wars: Battle of the Vosges against Ariovistus (58 BC)
wars.outcome: Caesar, at the Aedui's request, defeated the coalition of Ariovistus, who 'escaped across the Rhine'; the Sequani's ascendancy 'among the peoples of eastern Gaul' was broken and Labienus's two legions wintered in their territory.

certainty.note: The Jura and the Saone are the limits the page gives; the Rhine side is undefined.
